headline: BLAST condemns attack and demolition of Mirpur's Radda health centre
summary: The legal aid organization calls for a prompt and impartial investigation into the vandalism of the facility that served disadvantaged communities since 1974.
details: The Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) has expressed deep concern over the attack, looting, vandalism, and subsequent demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1.
In a statement issued on Sunday, BLAST described the assault as more than just property destruction, noting that it disrupted essential healthcare access for low-income and disadvantaged communities.
The organization urged authorities to identify all those involved, both directly and indirectly, and take appropriate legal action against them.
Established in 1974, the Radda MCH-FP Centre provided critical maternal and child healthcare, vaccinations, reproductive health, and family planning services.
BLAST emphasized that the closure of the facility has severely impacted a large number of residents who relied on these essential services.
The organization also called for the immediate restoration of the centre's damaged infrastructure and the replacement of lost equipment and assets.
caption:
A healthcare facility serving the poor since 1974 was looted and demolished. BLAST is now demanding justice.

The Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) has expressed deep concern over the attack, looting, vandalism, and subsequent demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1.

In a statement issued on Sunday, BLAST described the assault as more than just property destruction, noting that it disrupted essential healthcare access for low-income and disadvantaged communities.

The organization urged authorities to identify all those involved, both directly and indirectly, and take appropriate legal action against them.

Established in 1974, the Radda MCH-FP Centre provided critical maternal and child healthcare, vaccinations, reproductive health, and family planning services.

BLAST emphasized that the closure of the facility has severely impacted a large number of residents who relied on these essential services.

The organization also called for the immediate restoration of the centre's damaged infrastructure and the replacement of lost equipment and assets.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: Metro official embarrassed after [[athlete stopped for wearing shorts]]
headline: Metro official embarrassed after athlete stopped for wearing shorts
summary: A triathlete was allegedly harassed and called 'obscene' by police at a Dhaka Metro Rail station for his athletic attire.
details: Triathlete Sajjad Hossain Snigdho was allegedly stopped from entering a metro rail station on Sunday after a police officer called his athletic shorts 'obscene'.
Sajjad reported that he had been training at Ramna Park and was attempting to travel to Zia Udyan for another session when he was intercepted at the Farmgate station.
He alleged that officers laughed at him, harassed him, and took photographs of him while refusing him entry based on his clothing.
Sajjad claimed that a metro staff member told him that such attire 'doesn't go with Bangladesh' and that superiors backed the officers' position.
After being detained at the station for nearly 40 minutes, senior officials eventually granted him permission to travel.
Major (retd) Mohammad Zakir Siddique, deputy general manager (security) of DMTCL, stated that the authorities are embarrassed by the incident.
Siddique added that the authorities have taken note of the matter and will discuss it with the managing director to take necessary action following a written complaint.
